skills.description: Patterns and timed problem solving aligned to Google phone and onsite coding rounds.
skills.target: 145 curated problems across 24 weeks with Saturday retention tests.

modules.title: Foundations: arrays, hashing, two pointers
modules.overview: Build automatic recognition for linear scans, hash maps, and sorted two-pointer moves—the highest-frequency phone screen building blocks.
modules.whyGoogle: Most Google screens start medium-easy on arrays/strings; speed and clean invariants here save onsite energy.
learnItems: Hash map complement and frequency templates
Two pointers on sorted arrays and palindromes
Sliding window distinct vs at-most-K variants
When to sort vs when hashing wins
checklist: Solve Two Sum and 3Sum without hints
Explain duplicate handling in 3Sum
Code longest substring without repeating chars in one pass
State complexities before coding on a new problem
modules.youtubeSearch: NeetCode arrays hashing two pointers playlist

modules.title: Core structures: stacks, heaps, binary search
modules.overview: Monotonic stacks, priority queues, and binary search templates including search on answer for scheduling-style questions.
modules.whyGoogle: Google infra problems often reduce to heaps (top-K) or binary search on monotonic feasibility.
learnItems: Monotonic stack for next greater element
Feasibility check functions for BS on answer
checklist: Implement Koko Eating Bananas from scratch
Solve Meeting Rooms II with heap and explain sweep alternative
Find first/last position in sorted array
Articulate monotonic property before BS on answer

modules.title: Trees, graphs, and topological reasoning
modules.overview: DFS/BFS on trees and graphs, union-find, topo sort, and weighted shortest paths for onsite depth.
modules.whyGoogle: Graph modeling (dependencies, grids, connectivity) is disproportionately common in Google loops.
learnItems: Tree DFS: path, diameter, BST validation
Graph BFS for shortest unweighted paths
checklist: Draw BFS vs DFS choice for Word Ladder
Code Course Schedule II and explain cycle detection
Implement Number of Islands both DFS and BFS
Walk through Network Delay Time priority queue steps

modules.title: DP, greedy proofs, and hard follow-ups
modules.overview: 1D/2D DP, knapsack, LIS, interval greedy, and communicating optimizations under time pressure.
modules.whyGoogle: Onsite rounds extend mediums into DP or greedy proof sketches—partial progress needs clear narration.
checklist: Write edit distance recurrence before table
Solve LIS with patience sorting
Explain why greedy works for non-overlapping intervals
Practice one hard DP (Burst Balloons or Regex) with bounds

skills.description: Language fluency for Google-style backend interviews and clean on-the-fly implementation.
skills.target: The whole Go bank in teaching order — basics and data types first, concurrency once the language is solid, services and code comprehension last.

modules.title: Language basics: values, flow, functions
modules.overview: Zero values, the one loop keyword, functions as values, constants with iota, and how a package is laid out. Everything later in the track assumes this is automatic.
modules.whyGoogle: Nothing costs more interview time than fumbling declaration and loop syntax while also thinking about the algorithm.
learnItems: var vs := and the zero value of every built-in type
for as the only loop; if with an init statement
Multiple returns, the (T, error) convention, and closures
Constants, iota enums, and exported vs unexported names
checklist: Write a package with an exported constructor and an iota enum
Explain why a nil map reads but does not write
Return and handle (value, error) without a helper
Say what a closure captures inside a loop
modules.youtubeSearch: Go basics variables loops functions tutorial

modules.title: Data types: strings, arrays, slices, maps
modules.overview: Numeric conversion and overflow, runes vs bytes, how a slice header differs from an array, append growth, and map existence checks — the types every DSA answer is built from.
modules.whyGoogle: Interviewers accept Go if you are fluent; awkward slice handling costs credibility before the algorithm is even judged.
learnItems: Explicit numeric conversion and the overflow-safe midpoint
Range over a string with rune awareness
Arrays copy, slices alias: len, cap and append growth
Two-value map lookup and sort.Slice comparators
checklist: Implement two-sum in Go with a one-pass map
Use sort.Slice for an interval problem
Show two slices sharing a backing array, then break it with copy
Explain integer division and truncation
modules.youtubeSearch: Go slices maps runes interview coding

modules.title: Structs, interfaces, errors, and generics
modules.overview: Pointer vs value receivers, embedding instead of inheritance, small interfaces satisfied implicitly, error values with wrapping, and type parameters where they genuinely remove duplication.
modules.whyGoogle: Design discussions assume idiomatic error propagation and interfaces small enough to fake in a test.
learnItems: When a receiver must be a pointer
Implicit satisfaction, type assertions, and io.Reader
errors.Is / errors.As, and defer, panic, recover
checklist: Write a tiny LRU or min-stack API with a constructor
Return a wrapped error and match it with errors.Is
Explain nil interface vs typed nil pointer
Write one generic helper and justify it over a concrete one
modules.youtubeSearch: Go interfaces errors generics best practices

modules.title: Testing: table-driven, fakes, benchmarks
modules.overview: Table-driven tests with subtests, faking a dependency through the interface it already satisfies, and reading a benchmark or a pprof profile without guessing.
modules.whyGoogle: A take-home without tests reads as unfinished, and "how would you test this?" is a standard follow-up.
learnItems: Faking a small interface instead of mocking a framework
go test -race, -cover and what each actually proves
Benchmarks and a first pprof read
checklist: Add two table tests including the edge cases
Replace one dependency with a hand-written fake
Run a benchmark and explain the allocation count
Say what a test that only asserts no error is worth
modules.youtubeSearch: Go table driven tests benchmarks pprof

modules.title: Concurrency: goroutines, channels, context
modules.overview: Goroutines over the scheduler model, unbuffered vs buffered channels, select, the sync primitives, then context cancellation, worker pools and errgroup once the primitives are solid.
modules.whyGoogle: Go roles expect sane talk about goroutines and cancellation even when the coding round stays sequential.
learnItems: Buffered vs unbuffered channels and happens-before
select with context.Done, and mutex vs channel
Worker pool and errgroup with cancellation
checklist: Sketch a parallel URL fetcher with a timeout
Reproduce a data race and find it with -race
Explain when NOT to use goroutines in an interview
Pair with the Fundamentals OS threads module
modules.youtubeSearch: Go concurrency interview worker pool context

modules.title: Services: net/http and database/sql
modules.overview: A handler, a middleware chain, JSON in and out with validation, httptest against real handlers, graceful shutdown — then the connection pool, NULL handling and transactions underneath it.
modules.whyGoogle: The backend take-home and the "walk me through your service" follow-up both live here.
learnItems: Server, HandlerFunc, and a middleware chain
JSON encoding, validation, and error responses
httptest for handlers, and graceful shutdown
database/sql pooling, sql.Null types, and transactions
checklist: Ship one endpoint with middleware, tests and a timeout
Handle a nullable column without a panic
Explain an isolation level to a non-specialist
Shut the server down without dropping in-flight requests

modules.title: Operations and reading code you did not write
modules.overview: Twelve-factor configuration, structured logging with slog, health and readiness, a multi-stage image — then the comprehension drills: read an unfamiliar codebase, debug by hypothesis, and verify what an assistant hands you.
modules.whyGoogle: The 2026 loop includes a code-comprehension round, and operational judgement is what separates L3 from L4 answers.
learnItems: Config from the environment, never from a committed file
Structured logging with log/slog and request context
Health vs readiness, and a multi-stage Docker build
Reading an unfamiliar codebase fast; debugging by hypothesis
checklist: Read a 300-line unfamiliar package aloud in 45 minutes
Find one bug by hypothesis, not by printf roulette
Take an assistant’s patch and verify it line by line
Improve code you did not write without rewriting it
modules.youtubeSearch: Go slog configuration docker multi-stage code reading

skills.description: OS, memory, and runtime concepts that underpin design and coding follow-ups.
skills.target: Crisp explanations for threads, memory hierarchy, and process lifecycle without buzzwords.

modules.title: Processes, threads, and scheduling
modules.overview: How CPU time is shared, why goroutines map to threads, and where context switches hurt.
modules.whyGoogle: Latency and tail issues often trace back to scheduling and lock contention.
learnItems: Go scheduler M:N model at high level
checklist: Explain why busy-wait is bad
Describe race vs data race
Connect to Go concurrency module
Give one real incident tied to thread pool exhaustion

modules.title: Memory hierarchy and allocation
modules.overview: Stack vs heap, cache locality, and why allocation rate affects GC in Go and JVM languages.
modules.whyGoogle: Performance discussions at Google often mention allocation, caching, and profiling.
learnItems: Big-O vs constant factors at scale
checklist: Explain pointer chasing vs array scan
Relate slice append to realloc
Name one profiling tool you would use
Tie to DSA space complexity answers

skills.description: HTTP, DNS, TCP, and TLS vocabulary for design and reliability conversations.
skills.target: Explain a request path from browser to service with failure modes.

modules.title: DNS, HTTP/2, and REST shape
modules.overview: Resolution chain, connection reuse, status codes, idempotency, and pagination patterns.
modules.whyGoogle: API design rounds assume you know how clients actually reach services.
learnItems: REST idempotency for POST vs PUT
checklist: Walk DNS lookup steps aloud in 2 minutes
Design retry policy for idempotent GET
Explain 502 vs 503 vs 504
Link to Communication module for 6-min recording

modules.title: TCP lifecycle and TLS handshake
modules.overview: Three-way handshake, congestion idea, TLS layers, and where latency hides.
modules.whyGoogle: Global-scale services live or die on connection setup and cross-region RTT.
checklist: Draw TCP handshake
Explain why TLS adds RTTs
Describe SYN flood at high level
Connect to load balancer design week

skills.description: Structured design for L4+ loops: requirements, estimates, data model, and scaling paths.
skills.target: Two full designs per month with written postmortems and trade-off tables.

modules.title: Framing, estimates, and APIs
modules.overview: Repeatable opening: users, QPS, storage, read/write ratio, SLA, and API sketch before boxes.
modules.whyGoogle: Google design interviewers penalize jumping to Kafka without numbers.
learnItems: Read path vs write path separation
checklist: Practice URL shortener estimates in 5 minutes
Write API for create/read/delete
State three non-functional requirements
Time-box yourself to 35 minutes total

modules.title: Storage, indexing, and caching
modules.overview: SQL vs NoSQL choice, sharding keys, replication, cache-aside, and invalidation pitfalls.

checklist: Pick sharding key for social feed

modules.overview: Apply framing to news feed, typeahead search, and distributed rate limiting.
